title: $\RHom$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$
statement:
Fix distinct primes $\ell,p$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a separated scheme $X$ of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and write $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ for its pulled-back ring object as in [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Put $D=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$, let $C=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$ be its full subcategory of bounded constructible complexes [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and write $\iota:C\to D$ for the inclusion. Assume that the ambient derived internal hom $H=\RHom_{\Lambda_X}(-,-)$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] carries pairs of objects of $C$ to objects of $C$. By [lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves] this hypothesis holds for $\Lambda=\underline{\cO}_E,\underline E$ with $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, and for $\Lambda=\underline{\Qlb}$, with the latter coefficient ring as in [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed].

Define the restricted derived internal hom
$$
H_C=\RHom(-,-):C^{\mathrm{op}}\times C\longrightarrow C
$$
by $H_C(K,L)=H(\iota K,\iota L)$, equipped with the assumed bounded constructibility. For morphisms $u:K'\to K$ and $v:L\to L'$ in $C$, its map $H_C(K,L)\to H_C(K',L')$ is the ambient map $H(\iota u,\iota v)$, regarded as a morphism in the full subcategory. Thus this is the restriction in both variables of the ambient bifunctor. For every fixed $K\in C$ the compatibility with inclusions is
$$
\iota\circ H_C(K,-)=H(\iota K,-)\circ\iota;
$$
its canonical comparison natural isomorphism has identity components.

proof.text: For $K,L\in C$, the preservation hypothesis supplies bounded constructibility of $H(\iota K,\iota L)$, so the stated object assignment takes values in $C$. In the three displayed $\ell$-adic cases the statement of [lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves] supplies exactly this hypothesis, for the same setting and the same ambient derived internal hom. No assertion of preservation for an arbitrary condensed ring is needed.

source.place: first paragraph: preservation hypothesis and its three coefficient instances

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], $H$ is a bifunctor $D^{\mathrm{op}}\times D\to D$. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], the morphisms in $C$ are computed in $D$. Hence the ambient map for $u:K^{\prime}\to K$ and $v:L\to L^{\prime}$ is a morphism between the stated objects of $C$. The identity law is $H(1_K,1_L)=1_{H(K,L)}$. For $u^{\prime}:K^{\prime\prime}\to K^{\prime}$ and $v^{\prime}:L^{\prime}\to L^{\prime\prime}$, the composition law is $H(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})\circ H(u,v)=H(u\circ u^{\prime},v^{\prime}\circ v)$, directly the ambient bifunctor law. These equalities hold in $C$ because its Hom-sets are the ambient ones. This constructs the restriction in both variables.

source.place: restriction in both variables; unit _section.md, paragraph defining restriction

proof.text: Fix $K\in C$. Both composites in the displayed compatibility send $L$ to the same ambient object $H(\iota K,\iota L)$ and $v:L\to L^{\prime}$ to $H(1_{\iota K},\iota v)$. Since inclusion leaves morphisms unchanged by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], the comparison has component $1_{H(\iota K,\iota L)}$. Its naturality equation is $H(1_{\iota K},\iota v)\circ1=1\circ H(1_{\iota K},\iota v)$, the identity law. The inverse comparison also has identity components.

source.place: last sentence: for fixed K the functor commutes with the inclusions
